brief.title: Harborline Medical Devices
brief.synopsis: Harborline Medical Devices sells implantable sensors through hospital networks in North America and EMEA. Leadership wants a single Salesforce org to run opportunity tracking, partner-managed implant registrations, and post-implant case work. An on-prem ERP already owns product master and shipment confirmation. Hospital partners will register implants from their own portals, and compliance limits each hospital's visibility to its own implant records. A new release train must ship monthly without freezing production customizations for days. You will recommend an architecture that balances integration decoupling, partner visibility, and safe release practice.

stations.prompt: How should Salesforce notify the ERP and two regional warehouse systems when an implant registration is confirmed?

probes.label: Must the outbound message include fields computed from related Account and Product records?
probes.answer: Yes. The warehouse needs a computed SKU bundle code and hospital account territory that are not fields on the Implant Registration object alone.

probes.label: How many external consumers must receive the same registration confirmation?
probes.answer: Three: the ERP plus two regional warehouse systems, each owned by a different operations team.

probes.label: What latency will hospital IT accept during the implant registration save?
probes.answer: The save must stay interactive; multi-second synchronous callouts during registration are rejected.

probes.label: Can Harborline purchase additional Salesforce API call packs this quarter?
probes.answer: API pack spend is frozen at the current entitlement for this quarter.

probes.label: Must MuleSoft own the fan-out before Salesforce can publish a registration event?
probes.answer: No MuleSoft ownership mandate was recorded for the registration confirmation path.

probes.label: Is Change Data Capture required instead of a custom platform event?
probes.answer: CDC is available in the org, but the open decision is how the computed multi-consumer notification is shaped.

probes.label: Does the CEO require Salesforce Flow screens for every registration?
probes.answer: No UI mandate has been issued for the outbound notification design.

options.label: Publish a custom platform event after Apex builds the registration payload
options.rationale: Publish/subscribe lets one computed message reach every warehouse and the ERP without coupling the registration save path to each consumer. Apex can assemble Account and Product fields before publish.

options.label: Enqueue a Queueable callout job per warehouse from the registration trigger
options.rationale: One outbound job per consumer ties registration processing to every warehouse and grows trigger complexity with each new subscriber.

options.label: Call each warehouse synchronously from an after-save Flow action
options.rationale: Three synchronous external round-trips during save break the interactive registration path and compete for the same transaction limits.

stations.prompt: How should hospital partner users gain access to implant registrations without seeing peer hospitals' data?

probes.label: Are hospital users on high-volume Experience Cloud licenses without roles?
probes.answer: Yes. Hospital partners use high-volume Experience Cloud licenses without roles and authenticate through each hospital's IdP.

probes.label: Must each hospital's users be restricted to Implant Registration records related to their hospital Account?
probes.answer: Yes. Peer-hospital visibility is a compliance failure even for read-only list views and API queries.

probes.label: Do hospitals share a single parent Account or separate Account trees?
probes.answer: Separate Account trees per hospital network with no shared parent.

probes.label: Can Harborline disable the API for all partner users?
probes.answer: Partners need API access for their own EHR adapters; UI-only lockdown was rejected.

probes.label: Should every partner user be made a Salesforce System Administrator temporarily?
probes.answer: Temporary admin access is rejected by compliance.

probes.label: Can restriction rules alone replace account-scoped sharing for partners?
probes.answer: Restriction rules are not configured for Implant Registration in this org.

probes.label: Is one Experience Cloud site without account mapping enough for all hospitals?
probes.answer: A shared site shell is planned, but account mapping for record access is still required.

options.label: Sharing sets matching Implant Registration to each partner's hospital Account
options.rationale: High-volume Experience Cloud licenses do not use the role-based sharing model; sharing sets grant access by foreign-key match on Account lookups so each hospital partner sees only related implant records, including through the API.

options.label: One public Experience Cloud page filtered by a Screen Flow picklist of hospitals
options.rationale: UI filters do not enforce record visibility; partners can still query or deep-link peer hospital records.

options.label: One public group of all partners with a criteria-based sharing rule
options.rationale: A single all-partners group collapses hospital boundaries, so criteria sharing still grants peer-hospital implant rows to every partner user in the group.

stations.prompt: How should Harborline structure environments and promotion so monthly releases do not freeze production customization for days?

probes.label: Is source control the system of record for metadata, or is production still edited directly?
probes.answer: Leadership wants source-driven development; production hot-fixes still happen today and must be absorbed into the pipeline.

probes.label: How many concurrent workstreams need isolated sandboxes each sprint?
probes.answer: Four feature teams plus one integration test stream need concurrent sandboxes each sprint.

probes.label: Is there a fixed monthly production cutover window?
probes.answer: Yes: the second Saturday of each month, four-hour window.

probes.label: Can Harborline buy Unlimited Edition solely for more sandboxes?
probes.answer: Edition change is off the table this fiscal year.

probes.label: Should developers share one Developer sandbox and overwrite each other's work?
probes.answer: Shared overwrite sandboxes already caused two lost weeks of work.

probes.label: Must every concurrent stream use a Full Copy sandbox?
probes.answer: Finance rejected five Full Copy sandboxes; Partial Copy remains available for integration test.

probes.label: Can unlocked packages replace source control for this release train?
probes.answer: Unlocked packages are allowed later; source control remains the system of record for this train.

options.label: Source-driven CI/CD with a sandbox strategy mapped to team streams
options.rationale: Sandbox strategy pairs source-driven daily work with isolated Developer sandboxes per stream and a shared integration sandbox, so four feature teams plus integration test do not collide before the monthly cutover.

options.label: Edit production directly and capture metadata with weekly Change Sets
options.rationale: Direct production edits and ad-hoc Change Sets freeze work during cutovers and lose an auditable promotion history.

options.label: One shared full sandbox where all teams develop until release day
options.rationale: A single shared sandbox collides concurrent streams and cannot isolate integration test from feature work.
